class.name: HTTPServer
class.brief_description: A node that hosts an HTTP server.
class.description: Listens for plain HTTP requests, parses them, and resolves each one in a fixed order: a directory mounted with [method mount_files] is tried first, then a handler registered with [method route], then the [signal request_received] signal, and a request nothing answered is finally served [code]404 Not Found[/code]. Handlers and receivers alike are given a [code skip-lint]foundry.http.server.HTTPRequest[/code] describing the request and a [code skip-lint]foundry.http.server.HTTPResponse[/code] to complete. By default all work happens on the thread that drives the server. While the node is inside the scene tree it polls itself every frame; a headless caller can call [method poll] directly instead. With [member use_threads] the accepting, reading and parsing of connections runs on a worker thread instead, while handlers, the [signal request_received] signal and every response are still run on the main thread from [method poll]; the observable behavior is identical either way. A connection is persistent by default: an HTTP/1.1 client may send another request on the same socket once the previous response has been written. The socket is closed when the client asks for it with [code]Connection: close[/code], when the request is HTTP/1.0 without [code]Connection: keep-alive[/code], when the request is refused, or when [member connection_timeout_seconds] passes without a byte moving in either direction. A request is checked against the server's limits before it reaches any handler. A body larger than [member max_request_body_bytes] is answered [code]413 Content Too Large[/code] without being buffered; more header fields than [member max_header_count], a header line longer than [member max_header_line_bytes], or a header block that does not end within [member max_header_block_bytes] are each answered [code]431 Request Header Fields Too Large[/code]. A request carrying both [code skip-lint]Content-Length[/code] and [code skip-lint]Transfer-Encoding[/code], or repeating [code skip-lint]Content-Length[/code], frames its body ambiguously and is answered [code]400 Bad Request[/code], because acting on either reading of it is what request smuggling relies on. A header line folded onto the previous one is refused the same way, since a recipient that honors the deprecated fold and one that ignores it read different values from it. A transfer coding on its own is answered [code]501 Not Implemented[/code], since no coding is decoded here. Every one of these refusals is written to the client and then closes the socket. [b]Note:[/b] The default bind address is the loopback interface, so the server is reachable only from the local machine unless another address is passed to [method listen]. This class lives in the [code]foundry.http.server[/code] namespace, so it is reached either by its fully qualified name [code skip-lint]foundry.http.server.HTTPServer[/code] or, after [code]import foundry.http.server[/code], by the bare name [code]HTTPServer[/code]. Without that import the bare name does not resolve.

method.name: get_listening_port
method.description: Returns the port the server is bound to, or [code]-1[/code] if it is not listening. Use this to discover the port chosen by the operating system after calling [method listen] with port [code]0[/code].

method.name: is_listening
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while the server holds an open listening socket.

method.name: is_using_threads
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the server accepts and parses connections on a worker thread. See [member use_threads].

method.name: listen
method.description: Opens a listening socket on [member port] at [member bind_address] and returns [constant @GlobalScope.OK] on success. Set [member port] to [code]0[/code] to let the operating system pick a free port, then read it back with [method get_listening_port]. With no argument the listener speaks plaintext HTTP. Pass server-side [TLSOptions] built with [method TLSOptions.server] to terminate HTTPS: every accepted connection completes a TLS handshake before its first request is read, and all traffic on it is encrypted. Each call sets the mode, so a later plaintext [method listen] clears any options an earlier HTTPS run used. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_ALREADY_IN_USE] if the server is already listening, [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] if [member bind_address] cannot be parsed or [param tls_options] is not server-side, and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE] if HTTPS is requested in a build without TLS support.

method.name: mount_files
method.description: Serves the files under [param root_dir] for every request path that starts with [param url_prefix]. [param url_prefix] must start with [code]/[/code], and a trailing [code]/[/code] on it is ignored, so [code]"/app"[/code] and [code]"/app/"[/code] mount the same way. The prefix only matches whole path segments, so [code]"/app"[/code] claims [code]/app/index.html[/code] but not [code]/application/index.html[/code]. [param root_dir] must name a readable directory; [code]res://[/code] and [code]user://[/code] paths are resolved to their location on disk. A registration that does not meet these conditions is rejected and no mount is added. A mount is resolved before any route, so a route can never shadow a file the mount holds. A path the mount holds no file for — including a directory — is left to the rest of the resolution: routes, then [signal request_received], then [code]404 Not Found[/code]. Only [code]GET[/code] and [code]HEAD[/code] are answered; any other method is refused with [code]405 Method Not Allowed[/code]. Responses carry a content type derived from the file extension, an [code]ETag[/code] and a [code]Last-Modified[/code] field. A request repeating either validator through [code]If-None-Match[/code] or [code]If-Modified-Since[/code] is answered with [code]304 Not Modified[/code], and a single [code skip-lint]Range[/code] request is answered with [code]206 Partial Content[/code], or [code]416 Range Not Satisfiable[/code] when the range lies past the end of the file. A request whose path resolves outside [param root_dir], whether through [code]..[/code], percent-escapes, an empty path segment, or a symbolic link leaving the directory, is answered with [code]403 Forbidden[/code] and the file is never opened. A path carrying a backslash or an escaped control character is refused the same way, so a request can never name one file and reach another. Such a request is refused whether or not anything exists at the escaping path, so a mount cannot be used to probe the rest of the filesystem, and the refusal is final: it never falls through to a route or to [signal request_received]. If several mounts match a path, the first one registered claims it.

method.name: poll
method.description: Advances the server for one pass. In the default mode it accepts pending connections, parses whatever arrived, dispatches completed requests and writes pending responses. With [member use_threads] the worker thread already does the accepting, parsing and writing, so this only dispatches the requests the worker has finished parsing. Either way handlers and the [signal request_received] signal run here, on the calling thread. Called automatically once per frame while the node is inside the scene tree. Does nothing if the server is not listening in the default mode.

method.name: route
method.description: Registers [param handler] for requests whose method equals [param method] and whose path equals [param path] exactly, with the query string excluded. [param method] is matched case-insensitively; [param path] must start with [code]/[/code]. The handler is called with the request and the response as its two arguments. If several handlers are registered for the same method and path, the first registration wins. A routed request does not reach [signal request_received] unless [member emit_for_all] is enabled.

method.name: set_use_threads
method.description: Sets whether the server accepts and parses connections on a worker thread. See [member use_threads]. Calling this while the server is listening is rejected and leaves the property unchanged.

method.name: stop
method.description: Closes the listening socket and every open connection. In threaded mode the worker thread is stopped and joined first, so no connection is being read while it is torn down. Does nothing if the server is not listening.

members.member: The address [method listen] binds to. Defaults to the loopback interface, so the server is reachable only from the local machine. Use [code]"*"[/code] to accept connections on every interface. An empty value is rejected and leaves the property unchanged.

If [code]true[/code], [signal request_received] is emitted for every request, including the ones a route already handled. Receivers then run after the route handler, so the response is usually already committed, and a receiver that tries to complete it again is refused: the body, the status and the header fields are all fixed at that point. Such a receiver is an observer of routed traffic, not a second author of the response. If [code]false[/code], the signal is emitted only for requests no route claimed, which keeps routed traffic off the signal.

How many seconds a connection may go without moving a byte in either direction before it is dropped. The measure is progress, not age, so a large download is never cut off for taking many polls to deliver; what it does end is a socket that never sends a request, one that announces a body and then stalls, and one kept open after its last response. Set to [code]0.0[/code] to disable the drop entirely, which leaves a stalled peer holding its slot until it disconnects. Negative values are rejected and leave the property unchanged.

How many connections the server owns at once. A connection arriving while the cap is reached is left waiting in the operating system's listen queue rather than accepted and refused, so it costs the server nothing and is taken as soon as a slot frees. Must be at least [code]1[/code]; smaller values are rejected and leave the property unchanged.

The largest header block, request line and every field together, that is read for one request. A block that has not ended by this point never will, because nothing further is read into it, so the request is answered [code]431 Request Header Fields Too Large[/code]. This bounds what one connection can hold before its request is even framed, so raising [member max_header_count] or [member max_header_line_bytes] without raising this has no effect. Must be at least [code]1[/code].

The largest number of header fields one request may carry. A request carrying more is answered [code]431 Request Header Fields Too Large[/code]. Must be between [code]1[/code] and [code]255[/code]; other values are rejected and leave the property unchanged.

The largest single header field line, counting its name, its colon, its value and the terminating line break. A request carrying a longer one is answered [code]431 Request Header Fields Too Large[/code]. Must be at least [code]1[/code].

The largest request body, in bytes, that is read into memory and handed to a handler. A request announcing a longer body is answered [code]413 Content Too Large[/code] before any of that body is buffered, so an oversized request costs nothing to refuse. Must be at least [code]1[/code].

The TCP port [method listen] binds to. Must be between [code]0[/code] and [code]65535[/code]; values outside that range are rejected and leave the property unchanged. [code]0[/code] asks the operating system for a free port.

If [code]true[/code], [method listen] starts a worker thread that accepts connections and reads and parses their requests, off the main thread. Handlers, the [signal request_received] signal and every response are still run on the main thread when [method poll] drains the parsed requests, so nothing script sees changes; only where the socket reading happens does. Must be set before [method listen]; changing it while the server is listening is rejected. The default [code]false[/code] runs the whole loop on the polling thread.

signal.name: request_received
signal.description: Emitted for a request no route claimed, and for every request once [member emit_for_all] is enabled. A receiver completes [param response] the same way a route handler does; if none of them does, the request is answered with [code]404 Not Found[/code].
